title: 2021 ACC/AHA/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain

definitions.Typical Angina: Substernal chest discomfort; precipitated by exertion or emotional stress; relieved by rest or nitrates
definitions.High-sensitivity Troponin (hs-cTn): Detects myocardial injury at low concentrations; enables faster rule-out
definitions.HEART Score: History(0–2), ECG(0–2), Age(0–2), Risk factors(0–2), Troponin(0–2); ≤3=low, 4–6=moderate, ≥7=high

recommendations.text: 12-lead ECG should be obtained and interpreted within 10 minutes of emergency department arrival for patients presenting with possible ACS.
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) testing is recommended at 0h and 1–2h (accelerated protocol) for early rule-in and rule-out of NSTEMI.
Risk stratification using validated tools (HEART, TIMI, GRACE) is recommended to guide management of chest pain in the ED.
Patients with low HEART score (≤3) and normal hs-cTn can be discharged safely without further observation.
CCTA is recommended as a first-line diagnostic test for patients with stable chest pain of intermediate probability of obstructive CAD.
Exercise ECG testing is reasonable for evaluation of chest pain with intermediate probability when CCTA or functional testing is not available.
Stress MPI or echocardiography is reasonable as initial testing in patients with LBBB or paced rhythm, where ECG interpretation is limited.
Routine coronary angiography is not recommended in patients with chest pain and low probability of CAD.
Measurement of coronary artery calcium (CAC) may be considered in asymptomatic adults 40–75 years with intermediate ASCVD risk to refine risk stratification.

diagnostic_pathways.STEMI_pathway: ECG within 10 min → STEMI identified → activate cath lab → primary PCI within 90 min door-to-balloon
diagnostic_pathways.NSTE_ACS_pathway: ECG + hs-cTnI at 0h/1–2h → risk score (HEART/GRACE) → stratify: low (discharge), moderate (observation), high (early invasive)
diagnostic_pathways.stable_chest_pain: Pre-test probability assessment → if intermediate: CCTA first-line → if CCTA positive: functional test or ICA
